top_choice_rationale: A two-name prize to Katori and Ye for optical lattice clocks rests on a separable idea, the magic-wavelength lattice that cancels the differential light shift while holding many atoms Doppler- and recoil-free. The resulting 1e-18 performance is quantitatively understood and independently reproduced across laboratories, and the credit follows the record. The citation names the lattice, which keeps it distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes. The case rests on demonstrated capability, not on constants tests, which are still null. Awarding it is better than no award.
